news.headline: Another multimillion stock sale lined up for 2026 at Moderna (NASDAQ: MRNA)
MRNA Form 4 Filings - Moderna, Inc. SEC Form 4
Moderna (MRNA) CFO sells 34,836 shares under pre-set plan
Insider at Moderna (NASDAQ: MRNA) plans multimillion-dollar stock sale for 2026
Rothschild & Co Redburn Downgrades Moderna to Sell Despite Raising Price Target to $81
news.summary: Rothschild & Co Redburn cut Moderna to Sell from Neutral even as it roughly doubled its price target to $81 from $40, with analyst Simon Baker arguing that the market's reaction to the positive INTerpath-001 melanoma data was "beyond reconciliation under any plausible scenario" and left the stock considerably overvalued at its roughly $150 pre-downgrade close. Shares fell about 3% on the call, highlighting a growing analyst split between bulls citing the oncology and vaccine-approval momentum and bears flagging valuation.

news.headline: CDC Leaves Gap in Fall Vaccine Guidance, Doesn't Address New mRNA Flu Shot
news.summary: The CDC issued no new recommendations for this fall's COVID-19 or RSV vaccines and simply carried over last year's flu guidance, which does not mention Moderna's newly approved mRNA flu vaccine mFlusiva at all. Because ACIP has lacked a quorum since a March 2026 court ruling froze member appointments, medical groups such as the AAP and IDSA have issued their own vaccine advice, leaving insurance coverage and uptake of Moderna's new shots this season uncertain.

news.headline: Argus Upgrades Moderna to Buy With $180 Price Target
news.summary: Argus Research upgraded Moderna to Buy from Hold with a $180 price target, citing the recent run of FDA approvals that now give the company multiple approved mRNA products across COVID-19, flu and RSV. The upgrade capped a string of bullish analyst actions following the melanoma vaccine data and vaccine approvals earlier in August, underscoring a sharp divide with subsequent bearish valuation calls like Rothschild's.

news.headline: BioNTech Halts Rival mRNA Colorectal Cancer Vaccine Trial, Dragging Moderna Shares Down on Platform Read-Across Fears
news.summary: BioNTech and Genentech terminated the Phase 2 BNT122-01 trial of autogene cevumeran in resected colorectal cancer after a DSMB found the study was unlikely to show benefit and flagged an overall-survival imbalance versus watchful waiting. Coming just a week after Moderna and Merck's positive melanoma vaccine readout, the news pulled Moderna shares down roughly 6% as investors questioned how broadly individualized mRNA cancer vaccines can work across tumor types, though Morgan Stanley said the read-through to Moderna's melanoma program was limited.

news.headline: Moderna Prices Upsized $2.6 Billion Offering of 0% Convertible Senior Notes Due 2032
news.summary: Moderna priced an upsized $2.6 billion private placement of zero-coupon convertible senior notes maturing 2032, with a $400 million greenshoe option and a conversion price of about $210.58 per share, a roughly 47.5% premium to the last sale price. Net proceeds of about $2.56 billion are earmarked for general corporate purposes, including funding the growing oncology business and debt repayment.

news.headline: Merck and Moderna Announce Phase 3 INTerpath-001 Trial Met Endpoints in Resected Melanoma
news.summary: The Phase 3 INTerpath-001 trial showed intismeran autogene (mRNA-4157) plus Keytruda significantly improved recurrence-free and distant metastasis-free survival versus Keytruda alone in resected stage IIB-IV melanoma, the first positive Phase 3 result ever for an individualized mRNA cancer therapy. Shares initially rallied as much as 177% before giving back much of the gain within days on profit-taking and platform-risk concerns; Merck and Moderna plan to present full data at an upcoming medical meeting and engage regulators on a filing.

catalysts.label: ESMO Congress 2026 (Berlin) - full INTerpath-001 data presentation
catalysts.detail: Merck and Moderna said they plan to present full results from the positive Phase 3 INTerpath-001 melanoma trial at an upcoming international oncology meeting; ESMO Congress 2026, running October 16-20 in Berlin, is the most likely venue given timing, though no specific date or venue has been confirmed as of mid-September. Depth of the survival benefit, subgroup consistency and safety detail beyond the August 19 topline will shape how durable the oncology-driven re-rating in the stock proves to be, and will feed directly into the ongoing bull/bear valuation debate among analysts.

catalysts.label: Q3 2026 earnings report
catalysts.detail: Moderna is expected to report Q3 2026 results around October 29, 2026, based on financial-calendar trackers; the exact date has not yet been formally confirmed via a company press release. The report should update actual fall-season vaccine uptake and revenue against the roughly $4 billion full-year cash-cost target amid the ACIP/CDC guidance gap, and give further color on the broader INTerpath oncology program (nine Phase 2/3 trials across melanoma, NSCLC, bladder and renal cell carcinoma) as well as the mCOMBRIAX flu/COVID combination vaccine's still-unscheduled U.S. resubmission.

catalysts.label: Fall/winter 2026-2027 respiratory vaccination season - commercial execution amid CDC/ACIP guidance gap
catalysts.detail: With updated Spikevax, mNEXSPIKE and the newly approved mFlusiva flu vaccine now cleared for the season, Q3 revenue is guided by management to represent roughly 55% of second-half revenue as the vaccination campaign ramps. However, ACIP's ongoing lack of quorum since March 2026 has left the CDC without new formal recommendations for COVID, RSV or flu vaccines (the carried-over flu guidance does not mention mFlusiva), creating real uncertainty around insurance coverage and uptake of Moderna's newest products this season.

catalysts.label: Regulatory filing for intismeran autogene + Keytruda in melanoma
catalysts.detail: Following the positive August 19 Phase 3 INTerpath-001 readout, Merck and Moderna said they would engage regulators on a filing submission for intismeran autogene plus Keytruda in resected melanoma; no specific filing date has been disclosed. An earlier accelerated-approval attempt in 2024 was rebuffed by the FDA, so the path and timeline for a full BLA submission remain a key open question for the oncology thesis.

catalysts.label: mCOMBRIAX (flu/COVID combination vaccine) U.S. BLA resubmission
catalysts.detail: Moderna withdrew its original U.S. application for the combination flu/COVID vaccine in 2025 after the FDA requested additional Phase 3 influenza efficacy data; the vaccine already holds EU marketing authorization (granted April 2026) for adults 50+. Moderna has said it intends to resubmit in the U.S. but has not given a timeline, and mFlusiva's approval in August 2026 was viewed as a needed precursor.

catalysts.label: Norovirus vaccine (mRNA-1403) Phase 3 readout
catalysts.detail: Moderna's Phase 3 norovirus vaccine trial did not meet statistical criteria for early success, and the company is enrolling an additional Northern Hemisphere season cohort to accrue enough cases, pushing the readout beyond 2026. This is one of the few remaining infectious-disease pipeline assets after the CMV vaccine program (mRNA-1647) was discontinued in 2026 following a missed primary efficacy endpoint.

pulse: Moderna's August 2026 re-rating on the landmark INTerpath-001 melanoma readout remains volatile and contested: the stock's record one-day rally partially reversed within days, an unrelated BioNTech colorectal-cancer-vaccine trial failure on August 28 dragged shares further on fears about individualized mRNA cancer vaccines broadly, and analysts are now openly split, with Argus upgrading to Buy ($180 target) on August 31 while Rothschild & Co Redburn downgraded to Sell (despite doubling its target to $81) on September 3, calling the post-rally valuation irreconcilable with fundamentals. Underlying vaccine commercials remain structurally weak (Q2 revenue of just $145 million, still net-loss-making) and financed partly through an upsized $2.6 billion convertible note offering, while a new near-term risk clouds the core respiratory franchise: with ACIP still lacking a quorum since March 2026, the CDC has issued no updated COVID/RSV guidance and rolled over old flu guidance that doesn't even mention Moderna's newly approved mFlusiva, clouding coverage and uptake for the entire fall vaccination season. Near-term attention centers on full INTerpath-001 data expected at ESMO (mid-October, unconfirmed), Q3 earnings (expected around October 29) which will reveal actual fall-season vaccine demand, and any regulatory clarity on a melanoma combination filing.
